source: Official Gazette of India, Acts No. 45 & 46 of 2023 (BNS 2023 & BNSS 2023)
notes: TODO: Sourced directly from parliamentary gazette text. Requires senior advocate cross-check before public deployment.

oldCode.title: Punishment for Murder
oldCode.description: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

newCode.title: Punishment for Murder
newCode.description: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Sub-clause (2) additionally covers murder by mob lynching / group on grounds of race, caste, community.
newCode.keyChanges: Mob lynching incorporated into Section 103(2) with minimum 7 years to death penalty.

items.nature: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Triable by Court of Session

oldCode.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
oldCode.description: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property...

newCode.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
newCode.description: Consolidates cheating offenses. Punishment remains imprisonment of either description for a term up to seven years and fine.
newCode.keyChanges: Section numbering consolidated under Chapter XVII (Offences Against Property).

items.nature: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Triable by Magistrate First Class

oldCode.title: Punishment for Rape
oldCode.description: Punishment for sexual assault not less than ten years, but which may extend to life imprisonment.

newCode.title: Punishment for Rape
newCode.description: Punishment not less than ten years, extendable to life imprisonment and fine. Section 69 additionally criminalizes sexual intercourse by deceitful means/false promise to marry.
newCode.keyChanges: Deceitful promise of marriage explicitly criminalized under Section 69.

items.nature: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Triable by Court of Session

oldCode.title: Causing death by negligence
oldCode.description: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.

newCode.title: Causing death by negligence (Hit and Run)
newCode.description: Section 106(1) provides up to 5 years for rash/negligent driving. Section 106(2) provides up to 10 years if the offender escapes without reporting to police/magistrate.
newCode.keyChanges: Stringent provisions for hit-and-run without reporting.

oldCode.title: Punishment for Theft
oldCode.description: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

newCode.title: Punishment for Theft
newCode.description: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or community service for petty first-time theft where value is under Rs. 5,000.
newCode.keyChanges: Introduces Community Service as an alternative sanction for petty theft under Rs 5,000 on return of property.

items.nature: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Triable by any Magistrate

oldCode.title: Sedition (Disaffection towards Government)
oldCode.description: Punished words, signs or visible representation bringing hatred or contempt towards the Government established by law.

newCode.title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
newCode.description: Whoever intentionally incites secession, armed rebellion, subversive activities, or endangers sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
newCode.keyChanges: The colonial term 'sedition' is dropped; replaced by acts endangering sovereignty, unity, and integrity with minimum 7 years to life imprisonment.

items.nature: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Triable by Court of Session

oldCode.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
oldCode.description: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence shall be reduced to writing by the officer in charge of a police station.

newCode.title: Information in cognizable cases (Electronic FIR & Zero FIR)
newCode.description: Explicitly codifies electronic communication (e-FIR) to be signed within 3 days, and statutory Zero FIR irrespective of territorial jurisdiction.
newCode.keyChanges: Zero FIR and e-FIR are now expressly codified into the statutory provision.

oldCode.title: When police may arrest without warrant
oldCode.description: Circumstances under which a police officer may arrest an individual without a magistrate warrant.

newCode.title: When police may arrest without warrant
newCode.description: Section 35(7) mandates that for offenses punishable by less than 3 years, arrest cannot be made without prior permission of an officer not below the rank of DSP if the person is infirm or elderly.
newCode.keyChanges: Prior sanction of DSP required for certain vulnerable arrests with punishment < 3 years.

oldCode.title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in 24 hours (Remand)
oldCode.description: Magistrate could authorize police custody only within the first 15 days of detention.

newCode.title: Remand procedure
newCode.description: Police custody of up to 15 days can now be granted in whole or in parts during the entire 40 or 60 days period of the maximum detention.
newCode.keyChanges: 15-day police custody can be spread across the detention period rather than strictly limited to initial 15 days.

oldCode.title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
oldCode.description: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail.

newCode.title: Bail in non-bailable offences & Undertrial relief
newCode.description: Section 479 of BNSS provides that first-time undertrial offenders who have spent one-third of maximum sentence shall be released on personal bond.
newCode.keyChanges: First-time undertrial offenders eligible for bail after serving 1/3rd (instead of 1/2) of maximum sentence.
